name: LX Factory
seoTitle: LX Factory by Train or Tram 15E: Port-Day Timing
tagline: A converted 1846 textile mill under the 25 de Abril Bridge, now full of shops, cafés, street art and a large bookshop.

description.short: LX Factory is a former textile mill in Alcântara, under the 25 de Abril Bridge, let to shops, cafés, restaurants and studios since 2008. Entry is free. It is 4.6 km from the cruise terminal, so take the train, tram 15E or a taxi.
description.full:
LX Factory is a converted 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara, under the 25 de Abril Bridge, now let to independent shops, cafés, restaurants and studios. It is about 4.6 km from the ship, over an hour on foot, so plan transport each way.

Getting there: walk 26 minutes west along the river to Cais do Sodré and take a Cascais-line train two stops to Alcântara-Mar, then walk a few minutes inland to the gate on Rua Rodrigues Faria. Alternatively, tram 15E runs from Praça do Comércio to the Calvário stop, about five minutes' walk away. A taxi from the terminal takes about 15 minutes. Allow around 45 minutes each way by walk and train.

Timing: shops open from mid-morning and many restaurants only from lunchtime, so arriving at about 11:00 means most places are open before the lunch crowd. Weekends are busiest, especially when the LX Market craft and vintage stalls run, usually from 11:00.

If time is short: walk the main street for the murals and shopfronts, spend 20 minutes in the Ler Devagar bookshop, set in a former printing hall with a bicycle sculpture suspended overhead, then stop for coffee or lunch. An hour and a half covers it.

What to skip: if this is your first and only few hours in Lisbon, the Baixa, Alfama and Belém come first. LX Factory is a design, shopping and food stop rather than a monument, and prices are closer to trendy city restaurants than to neighbourhood cafés.

To make a half day of it, walk about 15 minutes to the Pilar 7 Bridge Experience (check the lift status first), or continue west to Belém on tram 15E from Calvário.

Context: the site opened as a textile mill in 1846 and has been a creative quarter since 2008.
description.history: In 1846 the Companhia de Fiação e Tecidos Lisbonense opened a large textile mill here, in what became Lisbon's main industrial district along the river at Alcântara. Over the following century the buildings passed to other industrial users, including printing works, and much of the complex later fell out of use as industry left the city centre. In 2008 the site was relaunched as LX Factory, with the old halls, staircases and painted signs kept largely as found and let to design studios, shops, restaurants and offices. The Ler Devagar bookshop later moved into one of the former printing halls.
description.significance: Alcântara was Lisbon's factory district, and LX Factory is one of the few complexes there that was reused rather than demolished. For a visitor it is the most compact place to see contemporary Lisbon design, independent shops and street art together. It also sits on the same tram and train lines as Belém, so it slots easily into a day heading west from the centre.

directions.general: Located in Alcântara district beneath the 25 de Abril Bridge. Main entrance on Rua Rodrigues Faria 103.
directions.fromCruisePort: About 4.6 km west, over an hour on foot. Take tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to the Calvário stop, or the train from Cais do Sodré to Alcântara-Mar; taxi about 15 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Train: Cascais line from Cais do Sodré to Alcântara-Mar, then a short walk. Tram 15E to Calvário (about 5 minutes' walk). Buses 714, 720, 732, 738 and 760 stop nearby.
directions.parking: Free parking available on-site. Street parking in surrounding area.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Complex open daily; each business sets its own hours

seasonal.hours: Varies by business (shops from mid-morning; restaurants and bars into the evening)
seasonal.notes: LX Factory does not publish a single opening time. Many restaurants open only from lunchtime, and bars stay open later from Thursday to Saturday.

seasonal.days: Weekends (Saturdays and Sundays on the organiser's current calendar)
seasonal.notes: Times as listed by Visit Lisboa; dates are set by the organiser (lxmarket.pt). No food stalls.

admissionPrices.notes: Free to enter and walk around. Shops, cafés and restaurants charge as usual; the Ler Devagar bookshop is free to enter.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekdays from about 11:00, when most shops are open and before the lunch crowd. Weekends are busier, especially on LX Market days.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Arrive late morning so that shops are open. Wear comfortable shoes: some surfaces are uneven and upper floors are reached by stairs. Budget for city-centre restaurant prices. Belém is about 3 km further west, so take tram 15E rather than walking.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: 3–3.5 hours, including about 45 minutes each way by walk and train (about 15 minutes by taxi)
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Too far to walk from the terminal; use the train, tram 15E or a taxi. The main street is level, but surfaces are uneven in places and some upper floors are reached only by stairs.
combinableWith: Belém: Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower (tram 15E)
Cais do Sodré and the Time Out Market (train back)
tips: Take a Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré two stops to Alcântara-Mar, or tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to Calvário; walking from the ship takes over an hour.
Allow about 45 minutes each way by walk and train, or 15 minutes by taxi from the terminal.
Arrive around 11:00: shops open from mid-morning, but many restaurants only from lunchtime.
On LX Market weekends, craft and vintage stalls are added, usually from 11:00, and the complex is at its busiest.
The Ler Devagar bookshop is free to enter; look up for the bicycle sculpture suspended over the hall.
Pilar 7 Bridge Experience is about 15 minutes' walk away, but its lift is out of service and the viewpoint is 372 steps up.
To continue to Belém, take tram 15E west from Calvário rather than walking about 3 km.

highlights: Former textile mill founded in 1846, with factory halls and painted signs kept
Ler Devagar bookshop in a former printing hall, with a suspended bicycle sculpture
Murals and street art throughout the complex
Independent fashion, design and homeware shops
Cafés and restaurants, many with outdoor tables
LX Market craft and vintage stalls at weekends
Directly under the 25 de Abril Bridge

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Main street is level but uneven in places. Most ground-floor shops are step-free; some upper floors are reached only by stairs.
